title: introduce-client-contract-fallback-middleware-for-toolcall-headers-and-stream-fallback
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds gateway middleware that accepts legacy tool-call envelopes and a prefer-contract header for gradual client rollouts; introduces a beta header X-Redwood-Contract and docs on migration. Non-breaking by default; opt-in via header.
description:
Motivation and context: Several customers reported tool-calling failures when clients send legacy 'tool_call' envelopes without the newer 'toolInvocation' wrapper introduced in the v3 wire contract. We want a low-risk rollout path that avoids immediate breaking changes while steering clients to the new contract via opt-in and deprecation signals. This PR implements a gateway-side fallback middleware that accepts legacy envelopes, performs a deterministic coercion into the current runtime internal model, and emits deprecation telemetry. It also adds a prefer-contract header and a beta header so we can A/B test the stricter contract before turning off the fallback.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds client-contract-fallback middleware at the OpenAI-compat gateway, introduces two headers (X-Redwood-Contract: beta-v2 and Prefer-Redwood-Contract: v3), implements streaming-coercion for partial tool-call events to keep streaming stable, updates router and runtime adapter to accept the coerced shape, adds unit/integration tests for tool/function calling and stream reassembly, updates docs and migration guide, and wires deprecation signals into metrics and logs.

Checklist (automated + manual): - [x] Gateway middleware that recognizes legacy 'tool_call' envelopes and rewrites to internal 'toolInvocation' shape - [x] Streaming path handles partial frames and KV-cache passthrough during coercion - [x] Header handling: X-Redwood-Contract (for opt-in beta) and Prefer-Redwood-Contract (client preference) - [x] Emit deprecation.counter{client_version,route} and deprecation.event logs with sample payloads - [x] Unit tests for coercion edge cases (missing args, nested tools) - [x] Integration test against runtime adapter to validate tool call lifecycle - [x] Docs: migration guide + changelog entry - [x] E2E smoke in canary environment

High-level commits: - 'middleware: add contract fallback and header parsing' - 'streaming: support incremental tool-call coercion for partial frames' - 'adapter: accept coerced toolInvocation and preserve tool metadata' - 'tests: unit and integration coverage for legacy envelopes' - 'docs: migration guide and examples'

Changed areas (high level): - src/gateway/middleware/contract_fallback.rs (new) - src/gateway/headers.rs (parse X-Redwood-Contract and Prefer-Redwood-Contract) - src/runtime/adapter/compat_adapter.go (accept coerced shape) - src/streaming/frame_rewriter.py (handle partial tool-call frames) - tests/legacy_tool_calls.test.js (integration) - docs/migration/route-tool-calls.md (new) - metrics/emit_deprecation_metric.sh (new wrapper) - examples/client-examples/compat_headers.md (docs)

Review conversation (condensed): - Alessandra: "Please add a unit test for the case where args is a JSON string vs an object; coercion should preserve type and annotate source." - Priya (author): "Added tests and an annotation field 'coercion_source': 'legacy_tool_call' with enum values; kept it internal-only and not surfaced to users." - Dmitry: "I am concerned about latency added by coercion on hot paths — did you bench this?" - Priya: "Yes — microbenchmarks in middleware show median wall-clock +0.4ms per-request under synthetic load; added an opt-out via Prefer-Redwood-Contract header to bypass coercion for high-throughput partners." - Samir: "Streaming partial-frame handling looks good; please ensure backpressure semantics unchanged." - Priya: "Verified with E2E smoke and added comments documenting backpressure behavior; added an integration test that replays partial frames from old clients." - Alessandra: "Approved after addressing test and perf notes."

CI summary: - Initial push: CI lint failed (header parsing style) - Fixup push: lint & unit tests passed, one flaky streaming integration failed in CI on first run - Rerun CI: all checks green (unit/integration/e2e smoke) - Final status: pass

Migration and rollout plan captured in docs: - Step 1 (canary): Merge middleware behind feature-flag for canary region only; communicate opt-in header to partners - Step 2 (beta): Enable X-Redwood-Contract: beta-v2 to measure adoption and emit deprecation telemetry - Step 3 (prefer header): Add Prefer-Redwood-Contract to let clients opt out of coercion when they support v3 - Step 4 (decommission): After 90 days and adoption thresholds, flip default to strict parsing and remove fallback.

Telemetry and observability: - New metrics: deprecation.counter, coercion.latency.histogram, coerced.calls.total - Logs: structured deprecation.events with client.agent, route, and sample payload (sampled at 0.1%) - Dashboard: added 'Contract compatibility' panel to the API console showing legacy envelope rates by client version.

Security and correctness: - Coercion is sanitizing inputs: any ambiguous 'args' types are parsed but preserved as opaque strings when parsing fails; we do not execute or eval payloads. - Added unit tests to ensure maliciously shaped envelopes are rejected rather than silently accepted.

Docs and examples: - docs/migration/route-tool-calls.md explains headers, example curl commands (both legacy and new envelopes), and a recommended timeline for partners. - examples/client-examples/compat_headers.md shows how to set Prefer-Redwood-Contract and X-Redwood-Contract.

Merge notes: Squash-and-merge after approvals. This was merged to main on 2026-01-21 using squash. Release note added to changelog under 'compatibility'.

Why this is different from previous compat PRs: Instead of adding a server-side permanent mapping, this PR focuses on a time-limited, observable, header-driven fallback that keeps streaming semantics intact for partial frames and lets clients explicitly opt into strict parsing. The approach is intentionally conservative to avoid regressions in high-throughput production customers.
